units.title: Unit 1: Theme, Objective Summary & Text Structure

lessons.title: Lesson 1a: Finding Theme & Using Text Clues
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy ELA: Finding the Theme of a Story
lessons.reading: The theme of a story is the big life lesson it teaches (such as "Steady practice overcomes mistakes"). You can also make inferences by combining text clues with what you already know.

principles.title: Identifying Theme and Using Text Evidence
principles.summary: Theme is the big life lesson a story teaches, supported by character actions and text clues.

bank.passage: Maya squeaked her violin strings during rehearsal and forgot a measure. Instead of quitting, she asked her teacher for help and practiced slowly every night. At the concert, her song rang clear and sweet.
bank.prompt: What is the central theme of Maya’s story?
choices: Steady practice and asking help overcome setbacks.
Only lucky people can play music.
bank.answer: Steady practice and asking help overcome setbacks.
bank.explanation: Theme is the life lesson of a story. Maya’s hard work shows that persistence leads to success.

bank.passage: Leo found a wallet on a park bench with twenty dollars inside. He saw Mrs. Alvarez’s library card in it and walked straight to her porch to return it. She smiled and thanked him.
bank.prompt: What life lesson does Leo’s choice teach?
choices: Honesty is better than keeping what is not yours.
Never walk through a neighborhood park.
bank.answer: Honesty is better than keeping what is not yours.
bank.explanation: Leo returns the lost wallet instead of keeping the money, showing the theme of honesty.

bank.prompt: Which statement is a complete story theme instead of just a topic?
choices: True friends help each other in hard times.
bank.answer: True friends help each other in hard times.
bank.explanation: A topic is one or two words, while a theme is a full sentence stating a life lesson.

bank.passage: When the class garden wilted in July, Noah wanted to blame Sam. Instead, Elena made a five-minute daily watering schedule for everyone. Two weeks later, bright red tomatoes ripened.
bank.prompt: Which detail supports the theme that teamwork solves problems?
choices: Elena made a shared schedule that saved the garden.
The watering can was made of metal.
bank.answer: Elena made a shared schedule that saved the garden.
bank.explanation: Text evidence is a specific detail from the story that proves the main idea or theme.

bank.passage: Crow held a piece of cheese in his beak. Fox praised Crow’s shiny feathers and begged to hear him sing. When Crow opened his beak to caw, the cheese dropped into Fox’s mouth.
bank.prompt: What is the theme of this fable about Crow and Fox?
choices: Do not let fake praise trick your pride.
Foxes can fly into tall trees.
bank.answer: Do not let fake praise trick your pride.
bank.explanation: A fable teaches a moral lesson. Crow’s pride made him fall for Fox’s trick.

bank.prompt: What two things do you combine to make an inference while reading?
choices: Text clues and your own background knowledge
Only page numbers and cover art
Only the last word of the book
bank.answer: Text clues and your own background knowledge
bank.explanation: An inference is a smart conclusion made by combining clues in the text with what you already know.

bank.passage: As the boat left the dock, Sofia gripped the railing with white knuckles. She stared back at the shore and swallowed hard while her brother cheered.
bank.prompt: What can you infer about how Sofia feels on the boat?
choices: She feels nervous about leaving shore.
She is angry at her brother.
She captains the boat every day.
bank.answer: She feels nervous about leaving shore.
bank.explanation: Clues like white knuckles and swallowing hard show that Sofia is nervous, even without saying the word.

bank.prompt: How do supporting details help the main idea in an article?
choices: They give facts and examples that prove it.
bank.answer: They give facts and examples that prove it.
bank.explanation: The main idea is the key point, and supporting details are the facts that back it up.

lessons.title: Lesson 1b (Ohio): Theme vs. Summary in Ohio Stories
lessons.reading: In Ohio’s ELA standards, readers separate theme from summary. A theme is the life lesson, while an objective summary briefly retells the main events in order without personal opinions.

principles.title: Theme vs. Summary in Ohio & Midwest Texts
principles.summary: A summary retells key events in order without opinions, while a theme states the universal life lesson.

bank.passage: Johnny Appleseed walked across Ohio planting apple seeds in clearings. He shared saplings with pioneer families so orchards would feed newcomers for years.
bank.prompt: What is the theme of this passage about Johnny Appleseed?
choices: Generous actions today can help others for years.
bank.answer: Generous actions today can help others for years.
bank.explanation: Theme is the universal life lesson. Planting trees for future families shows generosity and foresight.

bank.passage: Johnny Appleseed walked across Ohio planting apple seeds in clearings. He shared saplings with pioneer families so orchards would feed newcomers for years.
bank.prompt: Which sentence is the best summary of this passage?
choices: Johnny Appleseed planted apple trees across Ohio to feed pioneers.
Apples are the tastiest fruit in the world.
bank.answer: Johnny Appleseed planted apple trees across Ohio to feed pioneers.
bank.explanation: A summary briefly retells the main facts of a passage without adding personal opinions.

bank.prompt: What should NEVER be included in an objective summary of an article?
choices: The main idea of the text
bank.answer: Your personal opinions and feelings
bank.explanation: An objective summary sticks strictly to the facts and main points from the text, leaving out opinions.

bank.passage: In Dayton, Ohio, Orville and Wilbur Wright tested gliders that crashed in the sand. Each time, they measured the wings, fixed the frame, and tried again until they flew.
bank.prompt: What theme do the Wright brothers’ experiments show?
choices: Learning from mistakes leads to great discoveries.
Sand dunes are too windy for gliders.
bank.answer: Learning from mistakes leads to great discoveries.
bank.explanation: The Wright brothers studied each crash and kept improving, showing the theme of perseverance.

bank.prompt: How is a story summary different from a story theme?
choices: A summary retells main events; theme is the life lesson.
A summary is one word; theme is ten pages.
A theme only lists character names.
They mean the exact same thing.
bank.answer: A summary retells main events; theme is the life lesson.
bank.explanation: A summary tells what happened in the text, while a theme explains the deeper message or lesson.

bank.passage: When floodwaters rose along the Ohio River, neighbors filled sandbags together all night. By morning, the strong wall kept every home on the street dry.
bank.prompt: What is the theme of this Ohio River story?
choices: Neighbors working together can protect their community.
Sandbags are filled with river water.
Houses near rivers are always blue.
bank.answer: Neighbors working together can protect their community.
bank.explanation: The neighbors united to build the sandbag wall, teaching a lesson about community cooperation.

bank.passage: The Ohio and Erie Canal opened in 1832, linking Lake Erie to the Ohio River. Canal boats pulled by mules carried farmers’ wheat to distant markets.
bank.prompt: Which choice best summarizes this paragraph?
choices: The 1832 Ohio canal let boats carry crops to market.
Mules are much smarter than horses.
Canals are fun places to swim.
bank.answer: The 1832 Ohio canal let boats carry crops to market.
bank.explanation: A good summary captures who, what, and why in one short statement using facts from the text.

bank.prompt: Which detail belongs in a summary of a story?
choices: The main problem and how it was solved
Every single adjective on page two
Whether you liked the cover art
A list of your favorite foods
bank.answer: The main problem and how it was solved
bank.explanation: A story summary includes the main characters, the central problem, and the resolution.

lessons.title: Lesson 1c: Informational Text Structures
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy ELA: Informational Text Structures
lessons.reading: Authors organize nonfiction in clear patterns: Sequence (first, next, finally), Cause and Effect (because, as a result), Compare and Contrast (both, however), and Problem and Solution.

principles.title: Recognizing Informational Text Structures
principles.summary: Spot chronology, cause/effect, compare/contrast, and problem/solution using signal words.

bank.passage: Both butterflies and moths have wings with tiny scales. However, butterflies fly during the day, whereas most moths fly at night.
bank.prompt: What text structure is used in this passage?
bank.answer: Compare and Contrast
bank.explanation: Compare and contrast shows how two things are alike and different using words like "both" and "however."

bank.passage: Because warm lake water evaporated into cold air, thick snow clouds formed. As a result, heavy lake-effect snow fell on Cleveland.
bank.prompt: How is this weather passage organized?
bank.answer: Cause and Effect
bank.explanation: Cause and effect explains why something happened and what resulted, using signal words like "because" and "as a result."

bank.passage: To plant a seed, first dig a small hole in damp soil. Next, drop the seed in. Finally, cover it with dirt and water it.
bank.prompt: What text structure is used in these planting steps?
bank.answer: Sequence or Chronological Order
bank.explanation: Sequence order tells steps from first to last using words like "first," "next," and "finally."

bank.passage: Sea turtles can mistake floating plastic bags for jellyfish and swallow them. To solve this problem, towns organize weekly beach cleanups.
bank.prompt: What text structure describes the sea turtle paragraph?
bank.answer: Problem and Solution
bank.explanation: Problem and solution states a difficulty first and then explains how people fix it.

bank.prompt: Which signal words show a cause and effect text structure?
bank.answer: because, therefore, as a result
bank.explanation: Signal words like "because" and "therefore" connect a reason (cause) to its outcome (effect).

bank.prompt: A biography told by dates from 1870 to 1903 uses what structure?
bank.answer: Chronological Order
bank.explanation: Chronological order arranges real events in the time order in which they happened.

bank.prompt: Which signal words point to a compare and contrast paragraph?
bank.answer: both, alike, however, unlike
bank.explanation: Words like "both" show similarities, while "however" and "unlike" show differences.

bank.prompt: Which text structure tells steps in order from beginning to end?
bank.answer: Sequence Order
bank.explanation: Sequence order lists steps or events one after another in the exact order they happen.

lessons.title: Lesson 2a: Similes, Metaphors, Idioms & Context Clues
lessons.reading: A simile compares two things using "like" or "as." A metaphor says one thing IS another. Idioms are sayings like "piece of cake" (easy), and context clues help you figure out new words.

principles.title: Similes, Metaphors, Idioms & Context Clues
principles.summary: Similes use like/as, metaphors say one thing is another, and context clues reveal word meanings.

bank.prompt: Which sentence contains a metaphor?
choices: The classroom was a buzzing beehive.
He ran as fast as a cheetah.
The fur felt like soft velvet.
bank.answer: The classroom was a buzzing beehive.
bank.explanation: A metaphor compares two unlike things directly by saying one thing IS the other, without "like" or "as."

bank.prompt: Which sentence contains a simile?
choices: The icy sidewalk was as slick as glass.
The library was a quiet cave.
bank.answer: The icy sidewalk was as slick as glass.
bank.explanation: A simile compares two things using the words "like" or "as."

bank.prompt: What does the idiom "a piece of cake" mean?
bank.answer: Something very easy to do
bank.explanation: An idiom is a phrase with a non-literal meaning. "A piece of cake" means an easy task.

bank.passage: The ancient clay bowl was so fragile that workers wore soft gloves so it would not shatter.
bank.prompt: Using context clues, what does fragile mean?
bank.answer: Delicate and easily broken
bank.explanation: Context clues are nearby words that help explain an unfamiliar word. "Shatter" shows fragile means easily broken.

bank.prompt: What does the proverb "Actions speak louder than words" mean?
choices: What you do matters more than promises.
bank.answer: What you do matters more than promises.
bank.explanation: A proverb is a traditional saying that gives advice. Real actions prove more than talk.

bank.passage: After hiking ten miles up the mountain, the scouts were famished and ate every sandwich.
bank.prompt: What does the word famished mean in this sentence?
bank.answer: Extremely hungry
bank.explanation: Hiking ten miles and eating every sandwich are context clues showing famished means very hungry.

bank.prompt: What does the idiom "let the cat out of the bag" mean?
bank.answer: Told a secret by mistake
bank.explanation: "Letting the cat out of the bag" is an idiom that means revealing a secret.

bank.passage: The beaver was industrious, working from sunrise to sunset to fix the log dam.
bank.prompt: Based on the sentence, what does industrious mean?
bank.answer: Hard-working and busy
bank.explanation: "Working from sunrise to sunset" is a context clue showing that industrious means hard-working.

lessons.title: Lesson 2b: Complete Sentences, Run-Ons & Homophones
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy Grammar: Fragments, Run-Ons & Compound Sentences
lessons.reading: Every complete sentence has a subject and a verb. Fix run-on sentences with a comma and a joining word like "and," "but," or "so." Watch tricky homophones like their, there, and they’re.

principles.title: Complete Sentences, Fragments, Run-Ons & Homophones
principles.summary: Every sentence needs a subject and verb; fix run-ons with a comma + conjunction and pick the right homophone.

bank.prompt: Which choice is a complete sentence instead of a fragment?
choices: The falcon dove toward the river.
bank.answer: The falcon dove toward the river.
bank.explanation: A complete sentence has a subject ("The falcon"), a verb ("dove"), and expresses a full thought.

bank.prompt: Which choice fixes the run-on: "It rained hard we stayed inside"?
choices: It rained hard, so we stayed inside.
It rained hard we, stayed inside.
Because it rained hard staying inside.
It raining hard we stayed inside.
bank.answer: It rained hard, so we stayed inside.
bank.explanation: A run-on joins two sentences improperly. Fix it with a comma and a conjunction like "so."

bank.prompt: Which sentence uses their, there, and they’re correctly?
choices: They’re parking their bikes over there.
Their parking they’re bikes over there.
There parking their bikes over they’re.
They’re parking there bikes over their.
bank.answer: They’re parking their bikes over there.
bank.explanation: "They’re" means they are, "their" shows ownership, and "there" names a place.

bank.prompt: Which sentence uses the correct relative pronoun for a person?
choices: The scientist who found the fossil spoke.
The scientist which found the fossil spoke.
The book who I read was great.
The bike whom I rode is red.
bank.answer: The scientist who found the fossil spoke.
bank.explanation: Use the relative pronoun "who" for people and "which" or "that" for things.

bank.prompt: Which sentence uses its and it’s correctly?
choices: It’s fun to watch a dog chase its tail.
Its fun to watch a dog chase it’s tail.
It’s fun to watch a dog chase it’s tail.
Its fun to watch a dog chase its tail.
bank.answer: It’s fun to watch a dog chase its tail.
bank.explanation: "It’s" is short for "it is." "Its" without an apostrophe shows ownership.

bank.prompt: Which sentence uses the present progressive tense for action happening now?
choices: The students are building a robot.
The students built a robot yesterday.
The students will build a robot.
The students build robots every year.
bank.answer: The students are building a robot.
bank.explanation: Present progressive tense uses "am," "is," or "are" plus a verb ending in "-ing."

bank.prompt: Which sentence orders the adjectives correctly before the noun?
choices: She adopted a small brown puppy.
She adopted a brown small puppy.
He found three round tiny coins.
They drove a metal old truck.
bank.answer: She adopted a small brown puppy.
bank.explanation: In English, size adjectives like "small" come before color adjectives like "brown."

bank.prompt: Which choice is a sentence fragment?
choices: Whenever the campfire crackles at night.
Sparks floated into the dark sky.
Dad roasted marshmallows on a stick.
The tent stayed warm all night.
bank.answer: Whenever the campfire crackles at night.
bank.explanation: A fragment is an incomplete thought. Starting with "Whenever" leaves the clause needing a main action.

lessons.title: Unit 2 Exam: Reading & Language Mastery
lessons.reading: Show mastery of similes, metaphors, context clues, complete sentences, and homophones.

principles.title: Similes, Metaphors, Idioms & Context Clues
principles.summary: Similes use like/as, metaphors say one thing is another, and context clues reveal word meanings.

bank.prompt: Which sentence contains a metaphor?
choices: The classroom was a buzzing beehive.
He ran as fast as a cheetah.
The fur felt like soft velvet.
bank.answer: The classroom was a buzzing beehive.
bank.explanation: A metaphor compares two unlike things directly by saying one thing IS the other, without "like" or "as."

bank.prompt: Which sentence contains a simile?
choices: The icy sidewalk was as slick as glass.
The library was a quiet cave.
bank.answer: The icy sidewalk was as slick as glass.
bank.explanation: A simile compares two things using the words "like" or "as."

bank.prompt: What does the idiom "a piece of cake" mean?
bank.answer: Something very easy to do
bank.explanation: An idiom is a phrase with a non-literal meaning. "A piece of cake" means an easy task.

bank.passage: The ancient clay bowl was so fragile that workers wore soft gloves so it would not shatter.
bank.prompt: Using context clues, what does fragile mean?
bank.answer: Delicate and easily broken
bank.explanation: Context clues are nearby words that help explain an unfamiliar word. "Shatter" shows fragile means easily broken.

bank.prompt: What does the proverb "Actions speak louder than words" mean?
choices: What you do matters more than promises.
bank.answer: What you do matters more than promises.
bank.explanation: A proverb is a traditional saying that gives advice. Real actions prove more than talk.

bank.passage: After hiking ten miles up the mountain, the scouts were famished and ate every sandwich.
bank.prompt: What does the word famished mean in this sentence?
bank.answer: Extremely hungry
bank.explanation: Hiking ten miles and eating every sandwich are context clues showing famished means very hungry.

bank.prompt: What does the idiom "let the cat out of the bag" mean?
bank.answer: Told a secret by mistake
bank.explanation: "Letting the cat out of the bag" is an idiom that means revealing a secret.

bank.passage: The beaver was industrious, working from sunrise to sunset to fix the log dam.
bank.prompt: Based on the sentence, what does industrious mean?
bank.answer: Hard-working and busy
bank.explanation: "Working from sunrise to sunset" is a context clue showing that industrious means hard-working.
